verdict_summary:
Broadly solid research with one hard refutation, one damaging misattribution, and one unflagged time-bomb. I probed 25+ endpoints; almost every measured number the researcher gave reproduced exactly on the wire (Overpass US shop=truck_repair = 272; taginfo 813/369/441/3; NY DMV 54,563; NJ MVC 1,167; Overture categories CSV 2,117; Overture S3 release 2026-07-22.0 with 16 place files). Overture's own docs table independently corroborates the 74,223,561 worldwide total to the row.

THE ONE REFUTED SOURCE — data.transportation.gov. Claimed "21 catalog matches for 'repair', all Takata airbag recall assets, zero repair-facility registries." Actual resultSetSize = 1072, and only 3 of the top 100 are Takata. The top 100 contains multiple genuine repair-facility registries the researcher missed, and I verified them live: Connecticut "Licensed Automobile Dealers And Repairers" (data.ct.gov/resource/apne-w8c6.json, 138 rows) is explicitly licenseId=PUBLIC_DOMAIN with license_num, license_type, license_expiration and geocoded columns — a cleaner licence position than the NY DMV set the whole plan leans on. Also live: NJ Private Inspection/Emission Repair Facilities (332), Maryland Certified Emissions Repair Facilities (151), Montgomery County MD Motor Vehicle Repair and Towing (2,473). One trap I defused: the NY "Vehicle Repair Shops Across New York State" hit (3,426) is typed "filter" and is just the RSB slice of nhjr-rpi2 — not a new source, do not double-count. The narrower claim that FMCSA/USDOT itself has no repair registry may still hold, but the evidence offered for it is simply wrong.

THE MOST DAMAGING ERROR — a license quote attributed to a page that does not contain it. The researcher cited https://docs.overturemaps.org/attribution/ for the verbatim claim that Places "contains no OpenStreetMap data and carries none of the share-alike obligations." That page contains zero occurrences of "share-alike" or "no OpenStreetMap." The sentence is real, but it lives at https://docs.overturemaps.org/guides/places/. The license conclusion survives — I confirmed the quote verbatim, and the attribution page's Places section independently lists only CDLA-Permissive-2.0 / Apache-2.0 / CC0-1.0 sources with no OSM and, unlike Base/Buildings/Divisions/Transportation, no "License for theme: ODbL" line. So the permissive-Places strategy is sound; the citation of record must be fixed before anyone relies on it.

THE UNFLAGGED TIME-BOMB. On that same Overture guides page, verbatim: "The categories property in the places schema has been deprecated and will be removed in the September 2026 release, replaced by the new basic_category and taxonomy properties." Every Overture count in the report (truck_repair 10,858, towing_service 21,870, tire_dealer_and_repair 42,817, automotive_repair 201,199) and the entire 2,117-row category CSV sit on a field with about two months to live. Build against taxonomy/basic_category and treat categories as a transitional cross-check only.

Two staleness/precision issues worth acting on. The Foursquare source.coop mirror is correctly licensed (Apache-2.0 confirmed on its own page) but shows "Last Updated 21 Aug 2025" with newest release 2025-02-06 — roughly 17 months stale, and ingesting it silently would violate the repo's observed_at rule; the Hugging Face copy is current (lastModified 2026-07-09) and is where NOTICE.txt actually lives, at the cost of a free gate (raw README returned 401, so the gate is real). And the Google claim is right but mis-cited: maps-service-terms has zero occurrences of "Place ID" or "ratings"; the indefinite Place-ID storage exemption is on the Places web-service policies page, which I confirmed verbatim.

Vindications worth recording. The suspicious-looking OSMF URL ending "_Guideline_Guideline" is genuinely correct — the plausible "fix" 404s. Yelp's prohibition is confirmed and now carries an explicit AI/LLM-agent clause. Overture Places having no opening_hours is confirmed from the canonical place.yaml, which even disclaims operating_status as an hours proxy. Foursquare's schema confirms no hours, no rating, no review count, while facebook_id/instagram/twitter and date_refreshed do exist — supporting both the WhatsApp-substitute and last_verified_date recommendations. TIGER/Line PRISECROADS is live with 56 state files, so the strongest structural recommendation in the report — build the routes table on public-domain federal geometry to avoid the ODbL derivative-database trap — survives verification intact. EPA FRS is real and fresh (1.355 GB, Last-Modified 2026-07-08). SAM.gov returns 200 but is an empty Angular shell whose entire visible text is "SAM.gov -->", so it should be downgraded to reachable-but-unverified and is in any case an entity-registration database, not a repair registry.

Net: the licensing architecture (permissive Overture/FSQ/ATP core, ODbL OSM quarantined in osm.*, public-domain TIGER routes) is correct and now verified from primary sources. Fix the two citations, add the September 2026 categories migration to the plan, prefer the Hugging Face FSQ release over the stale mirror, and re-run the USDOT catalog sweep properly — Connecticut's public-domain repairer registry alone justifies it.
